what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat mild to moderate COVID-19 in adults and children (12 years and older, weighing at least 40 kg) who are at high risk of getting very sick or being hospitalized from COVID-19. It works best when started as soon as possible after you test positive for COVID-19.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with or without food. Each dose includes THREE tablets taken together at the same time: TWO pink tablets (nirmatrelvir) and ONE white tablet (ritonavir). Swallow all three tablets whole — do not crush, break, or chew them. Take all doses even if you start feeling better, because stopping early may allow the virus to keep growing.
dosing: The usual dose for adults with normal kidney function is TWO nirmatrelvir tablets (150 mg each) PLUS ONE ritonavir tablet (100 mg), taken TWICE a day (once in the morning and once in the evening) for 5 days in a row. Your doctor may lower your dose if you have kidney problems. Always follow the exact instructions your doctor or pharmacist gave you.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been less than 8 hours since your scheduled dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it has been MORE than 8 hours, skip the missed dose and take the next dose at your regular time. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets in their original packaging. Keep out of reach of children. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: IMPORTANT — this medicine can interact with MANY common medications and may cause serious or life-threatening problems. Before starting Paxlovid, tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL medicines you take, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements. Common medicines that may need to be stopped or adjusted include certain cholesterol medications (like simvastatin or lovastatin), some heart rhythm medicines, certain blood thinners, some migraine medicines, and St. John's Wort. Do not start or stop any medicine without checking with your healthcare provider first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek emergency care right away if you experience: serious allergic reactions such as rash, hives, difficulty breathing, or swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat; yellowing of your skin or eyes (signs of liver problems); fast or irregular heartbeat; severe nausea, vomiting, or stomach pain; or any new or worsening symptoms. Also call your doctor if your COVID-19 symptoms come back or get worse after you finish the 5-day course, as some people may need a second round of treatment.
when_it_works: Paxlovid works best when started within 5 days of your first COVID-19 symptoms. It will not work if your symptoms have lasted longer than 5 days. You may start to feel better within a few days, but always complete the full 5-day course even if you feel well.
special_populations: Kidney problems: Your doctor may lower your dose if your kidneys do not work well. This medicine is NOT recommended if you have severe kidney disease. Liver problems: This medicine is NOT recommended if you have severe liver disease. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of this medicine during pregnancy is not fully known. This medicine may also make hormonal birth control pills less effective, so use an additional form of birth control (like condoms) during treatment and for 7 days after finishing the course. Children: Safety and effectiveness have not been established in children under 12 years old or weighing less than 40 kg (88 lbs).
